segments.text: Twelve boys and their coach walk into a cave. Then the rain comes, and the way out fills with water.
The water chases them deeper, up onto a slope of mud in the dark.
No daylight. No way back. Outside, divers fight the flood for nine nights.
Then a light comes up out of the water. Two British divers. All thirteen are alive.
But finding them was the easy part. The way out is underwater, through tight, twisting tunnels in a strong current.
One rescuer, Saman Kunan, dies carrying air tanks into the cave.
So the divers sedate each boy, fit a full face mask, and carry him out underwater, one by one.
Over three days, all thirteen come out alive.
Hours later, the pumps fail and the water rises again.
I was wrong. Thirteen in, thirteen out. Case closed. And it began the day
